title: commitwork monitor project registry
description: The registry read by monitor/registry.mjs. An AREA is the declared unit of report output, retention, freshness and picker identity; registry-entry to area is N:1 and DECLARED, never inferred from a sweep's contents. Enforced at runtime TWICE, at the same read boundary: validateRegistry() (wrong types die, unknown keys warn — except in `deploy`, where they die) and validateAgainstSchema(), which parses THIS FILE. Both are fatal in loadRegistry(); when the two disagree, the disagreement is the finding.
$comment: This file HAS a code consumer: monitor/registry.mjs validateAgainstSchema(), called from loadRegistry(). It did not until R15 — `grep -rn projects.schema --include=*.mjs` returned zero hits, so every constraint below was unenforced prose. Two consequences to keep in mind when editing. (1) A constraint added here now blocks every sweep, panel boot and rollup, because loadRegistry() is the single read boundary for monitor/projects.json. (2) The checker implements a SUBSET of draft-07 — type, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, pattern, enum, minItems, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, oneOf — and treats any OTHER keyword as an error rather than ignoring it. Adding $ref, allOf, anyOf, dependencies, format or const here will fail loudly until registry.mjs implements them. That is deliberate: silently skipping an unimplemented keyword is how a schema goes back to being decorative.

semgrepPro.description: Which repositories run the Semgrep Pro engine. Pro is licensed for a BOUNDED number of repos and this fleet resolves to 119, so the engine is allocated per repository (monitor/sweep.mjs sets $CW_SEMGREP_PRO per repo; the sast command in manifests/security-baseline.json expands the flag only when it is set) rather than fixed in the manifest. Repos outside the allocation run the OSS engine and publish REAL findings — the narrower engine is recorded as a coverage bound (scan-scope's `engine-per-repo` note), never as a reason to discount a number.

repos.description: Names of RESOLVED repositories (what resolveRepos returns and the sweep scans), not projects[] entries — measured 2026-08-29, 8 declared projects resolve to 119 repos and 112 of the scanned names appear in no projects[] entry. The CAP is not expressible here and lives in monitor/registry.mjs (SEMGREP_PRO_MAX), enforced by validateRegistry; the two checks are complementary, not redundant. Duplicates are likewise rejected there rather than by a `uniqueItems` keyword, because this validator treats any keyword it does not implement as an error — declaring one would make every registry unvalidatable instead of making duplicates illegal.

note.description: Why this particular allocation — which repositories earn a scarce seat, and when that was last revisited.

reportsRoot.description: Report tree root, relative to the commitwork checkout.

monitorOutput.description: DEPRECATED legacy single-area output dir, and DELIBERATELY UNSET in this repo's registry since 2026-08-06 — declare `primary: true` on an area instead. Still accepted (a reverted pre-areas[] binary reads it, and monitor/area.mjs keeps it as precedence rung 3), but setting it makes one area the fleet-wide default output dir and OUTRANKS areas[].primary, which is the defect Tranche 1.1 removed: an unscoped run wrote every project's numbers into that one customer's report directory.

areas.description: Declared output areas. At most one may be primary.

out.description: Report directory (reports/<out>/). Defaults to slug. DISTINCT from slug on purpose: the fleet is slug 'client-a' but out 'client-a-monorepo', and both are load-bearing in existing paths.

thirdParty.description: This area holds code nobody here owns. It is a MACHINE-READABLE ownership fact, not a scoping one: tools that would MUTATE a repo refuse on it. monitor/preflight-build.mjs --apply refuses to run a third party's resolver (gradlew, setup.py, cargo, bundler) on the host, because that is arbitrary code execution as the operator against code we did not write. Absence of a deploy/renovate block does NOT imply this — a library the fleet owns declares neither.

members.description: Repo/entry names belonging to this area.

prefixes.description: Name prefixes that resolve to this area (e.g. svc-, web-).

primary.description: The default area for unscoped views. At most one.

races.description: Run the races (concurrency) scan for this area.

cadenceMs.description: Expected sweep interval; the freshness deadman's per-area staleness threshold.

deploy.description: DEPLOYMENT DECLARATION — which hostnames this area answers on, backed by which local origin. Declaration only: bin/deploy.mjs generates a cloudflared ingress FRAGMENT from it; commitwork never holds Cloudflare credentials, never mutates DNS, never restarts a tunnel — applying stays a human step. A tunnel is per-BOX (one credentials file, one daemon, many projects) while this block is per-AREA, so the fragment is merged into a box-level config this repo does not own. A hostname may be claimed by ONE area only. UNKNOWN KEYS ARE FATAL here and only here (additionalProperties:false below, and validateRegistry() pushes an ERROR rather than a warning): the forward-compat warning that is right for areas/projects is wrong for the one block whose contents leave this tree as ingress applied to a launchd-managed tunnel with KeepAlive:true. A misspelled key is not a future feature, it is a key that does nothing — and `noTLSVerify`, `httpHostHeader` or a nested `originRequest` would be silently dropped from the fragment while the declaration still read as though they applied.

hostnames.description: Public hostnames this area answers on. Lowercase DNS names, at least two labels — these reach the generated ingress YAML verbatim.

service.description: The local origin URL behind the hostname(s), e.g. https://127.0.0.1:8099. http(s) only — parseable host:port is what the not-listening probe needs. REQUIRED unless hosting:'pages', and FORBIDDEN with it — a pages-hosted area has no local origin. That conditional is enforced by validateRegistry(), not here: the runtime subset checker refuses schema keywords it does not implement, and if/then would be exactly such a keyword, so the hand validator carries the rule and this description declares it.

hosting.description: Where the hostnames are served when NOT through the tunnel. 'pages' = Cloudflare Pages serves them: bin/deploy.mjs emits NO ingress rule (and says so by name — a tunnel rule would fight the DNS), the not-listening probe skips the area, and bin/probe-public.mjs still watches the hostnames from the same declaration. Tunnel-hosted areas simply omit this key.

public.description: May this origin be routed through the tunnel at all? false = declared but never emitted: visible in the deploy table, absent from the fragment.

requiresAuth.description: This origin must not be published naked. public:true + requiresAuth:true + NO authAt is REFUSED by bin/deploy.mjs (non-zero exit) — generated ingress carries no auth, so emitting it would publish an unauthenticated origin. The central safety property.

probePath.description: Path an availability probe asks for on these hostnames; defaults to "/". Declared because a hostname can serve a public front page and gate its app elsewhere — overwatch.example serves "/" anonymously by design and gates "/app", so probing "/" there reports a working gate as an absent one.

authAt.description: WHERE the required auth layer actually lives, and the only way to declare a published origin that authenticates itself. 'origin' = the service checks its own requests (the admin panel's password+TOTP front door); 'edge' = a proxy or Access policy sits in front. Setting it satisfies requiresAuth for emission, so it is an ATTESTATION and `bin/deploy.mjs --verify` re-checks it against the live origin rather than believing it. FOUR verdicts, of which exactly one passes (lib/deploy-core.mjs classifyAttestation): `protected` — the origin refused an unauthenticated request and the refusal was about identity; `unprotected` — it answered 2xx, so the claim is false; `unusable` — it refused because NOBODY can authenticate (zero operators in the store), which must never count as protection, since it is the failure state the attestation exists to detect; `unverifiable` — the probe got no answer, or authAt:'edge', which a loopback probe bypasses by construction. Only `protected` is silence. Omit the key and requiresAuth:true still refuses — absence must never read as 'auth exists'.

originServerName.description: Pin ONE TLS server name for every rule. Usually omitted: bin/deploy.mjs defaults it per hostname (the origin cert covers each public name), which is what per-hostname verification wants.

caPool.description: Path to the CA bundle that signed the origin cert (e.g. an mkcert root). Referenced in the fragment, never read or written by this repo.

renovate.description: Renovate DECLARATION for this area — which GitHub repository's Dependency Dashboard and PRs describe it. Declaration only: it names a repo, holds no token (gh supplies auth) and runs nothing on its own. Exists because monitor/renovate-status.mjs previously defaulted to a hardcoded 'Portll/client-a' with nothing setting the override, so EVERY area's Renovate row reported one customer's PRs. An area with no renovate block is a declared VOID — the snapshot records that nothing is declared and reports nothing, rather than substituting another area's repo (explicit uncertainty applies to WHICH repository a number came from, not only to whether one was scanned).

repo.description: GitHub owner/name whose Renovate state describes this area.

config.description: Optional path to the repo's renovate.json, relative to a discovered checkout. Absent means the config is not read — the dashboard and PRs still are.

bola.description: BOLA/authorization-testing DECLARATION for this area — which bundled bola manifest describes its accounts and object endpoints, and the LOCAL TESTBED base to probe. Declaration only, like deploy: it names the manifest and target; it holds no credentials (the manifest names env/keychain vars, resolved at run time by lib/secrets.mjs) and runs nothing on its own. The panel's BOLA tab reads this to decide which areas offer a run, and the check is READY only when every secret the manifest names resolves — else BLOCKED with the missing names (explicit uncertainty). base is a loopback/testbed URL on purpose: a probe never invents its target, and object-level testing seeds writes.

base.description: The running LOCAL TESTBED origin to probe (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080). Overridable per run by --base / CW_TARGET_URL.

minify.description: Per-area overrides for the minifiedCode lane (bin/minify-detect.mjs), exported to it as CW_MINIFY_* env when this area is swept. Lets a deliberately-minified static-site area raise its thresholds without blanket-suppressing the lane fleet-wide; the scanner echoes the effective values into its report, so a narrowed threshold is disclosed rather than silent. An explicit CW_MINIFY_* in the operator's environment still overrides these.

entropyRule.description: Enable the default-off entropy-blob rule for this area (CW_MINIFY_ENTROPY_RULE).

retention.description: Per-area retention, overriding the top-level `retention` for this area only (monitor/retention.mjs resolves it; monitor/compact-reports.mjs acts on it). The two axes UNION: a batch survives if it is among its area's newest keepFullSweeps OR younger than keepDays. Protection only ever adds, because the compactor deletes.

keepFullSweeps.description: Newest batches of THIS area kept whole, replacing the global count. 0 is legal and means the area relies on keepDays alone.

keepDays.description: Age floor in days, measured from the batch NAME's UTC stamp (never mtime — pruning rewrites mtime). A batch inside the floor keeps its CodeQL databases; the compactor never deletes a whole batch, so this is a database-retention window, not an evidence one.

rollupBatch.description: Which of this area's batches monitor/rollup.mjs rolls when none is named. 'newest' (default) is right for a one-repo area. 'newest-full' skips batches narrowed by --repo (manifest `only`) and takes the newest that swept the WHOLE area — for a multi-repo area, where a single-repo sweep landing last would otherwise publish one repo as the area's whole state. It REFUSES rather than falling back if no full batch exists.

paused.description: Area declared outside every AUTOMATIC sweep. Persistent, unlike --exclude, which is run-scoped on purpose. Both fields are required: an exclusion with no reason is indistinguishable from an oversight, and a pause that cannot say when it started cannot be reviewed. A paused area's freshness state is 'paused' — never fresh, and never the permanent expiry it would otherwise accrue.

projects.description: Explicitly declared registry entries. NOT required at the top level: a registry may declare only `roots[]` and let discovery populate it, and validateRegistry() has always treated this key as optional. This schema listed it under `required` until the wiring in R15 made the schema executable and the disagreement surfaced — eight fixture registries that load correctly would have been rejected. The hand-rolled validator was right; the schema was wrong and nothing could tell, because nothing read it.

area.description: Declared owning area slug. REQUIRED when areas[] is present.

path.description: ~-relative or absolute path to the checkout.

expand.description: Treat each child directory as its own scanned repo.

hermeticTest.description: What the repository's tests need on a bare runner, declared by the operator and never by the repository (bin/hermetic-test.mjs). prepare runs in the empty HOME before cargo test.

excludeReasons.description: Per-repo reason for an entry in `exclude`, keyed by repo name. A reason specific to some repos must not be stamped onto every exclusion; repos without an entry fall back to `excludeNote`.
